stances.claim: The most important element of speedy quality justice is the people -- justices and judges -- and 'industry' should be added to the four constitutional traits of competence, integrity, probity, and independence.
The four positive INs (INtegrity, INdependence, INtelligence, INdustry) are the judge-quality framework -- anyone who cannot devote at least 10 work hours daily does not deserve JBC nomination.
stances.rhetorical_move: mnemonic coinage with quantified minimum standard

stances.claim: The four negative SHIPs (kinSHIP, relationSHIP, friendSHIP, fellowSHIP) are the plague of the judiciary -- judges must cut their umbilical cords to family, classmates, fraternity/sorority, and compadres.
stances.rhetorical_move: negative-trait enumeration as a disqualification test

stances.claim: The JBC-IBP MOA signed on December 8 is a valuable tool for screening judicial applicants using the IBP chapters' local knowledge of candidates' character.
Ideally each judge should have only 100 cases -- achieving this would require 7,400 more trial courts and 7,400 more judges.
stances.rhetorical_move: ideal-vs-reality arithmetic to frame the scale of the problem

notable_anecdotes: The four negative SHIPs mnemonic: kinSHIP (blood relations), relationSHIP (romantic), friendSHIP (school/town/compadre ties), fellowSHIP (fraternity/sorority) -- a rhetorical coinage unique to this column.

The 7,400-more-courts arithmetic: with the ideal of 100 cases per judge, it would take 7,400 additional trial courts and judges to handle the 980,000-case backlog -- a figure that contextualizes why individual hard work cannot solve systemic overload.

JBC's 30th anniversary MOA with the IBP (December 8, 2017): IBP chapters to inform JBC of both favorable and unfavorable information on judicial applicants -- leveraging local knowledge for national judicial quality.
The JBC must screen 1,800 lawyers (or 3,600 for real choices) just to fill 600 vacant trial court seats -- a scale the column cites to explain why the JBC needs IBP's help.
target_audience: JBC members applying the screening framework

decision_framework_signals: Apply the four INs as the positive screening criteria and the four SHIPs as the negative disqualifying criteria for JBC nominations
Set a concrete minimum standard: 10 work hours daily as the floor for judicial candidacy
Use IBP local chapter information -- both favorable and unfavorable -- as a field intelligence layer in JBC screening
Acknowledge that filling vacancies in boondocks courts requires more creative recruitment than urban courts
Use the 100-cases-per-judge ideal as a planning benchmark even if the 7,400-courts solution is impossible -- it shows the scale
Require continuous education at the Philippine Judicial Academy as a non-negotiable career condition
one_paragraph_summary: On Christmas Day, Panganiban addresses the most important element of speedy quality justice -- the people, specifically the justices and judges. With 980,000 cases pending in 2,400 trial courts (an average of 408 per sala, some exceeding 1,000), plus several thousand in appellate courts and an average of 550 per SC member plus 50 new cases monthly, the problem demands more than hard work. He proposes adding 'industry' to the Constitution's four existing judicial standards -- competence, integrity, probity, and independence -- and memorializes the full package as the four positive INs: INtegrity, INdependence, INtelligence, INdustry. Anyone unable to commit at least 10 work hours daily does not deserve JBC nomination; 'a judicial career is not a walk in the park; it requires work, work, work.' He introduces the concept of the four negative SHIPs -- kinSHIP (blood relations), relationSHIP (romantic), friendSHIP (schoolmates, townmates, compadres), and fellowSHIP (fraternity/sorority) -- as the plague of the judiciary: judges must cut their umbilical cords to all of these. With only 75% of 2,400 trial courts occupied, the JBC must screen 1,800 lawyers (or 3,600 for real choices) to fill 600 vacancies; on December 8, the JBC signed a memorandum of agreement with the IBP (president Abdiel Dan Elijah Fajardo, EVP Domingo Egon Cayosa) under which IBP chapters will provide favorable and unfavorable information on applicants to help select 'the best, the brightest, the most competent and the most upright.' Achieving the ideal of 100 cases per judge would require 7,400 more trial courts and 7,400 more judges -- which is why reducing the avalanche of cases at inception is essential, to be taken up next Sunday.
